summary: ASTROBIO is an explainable health assessment prototype for crewed deep-space missions. When Mars communication delay reaches about 20 minutes one way, the crew must act before Mission Control can reply. ASTROBIO brings measurements for NASA's five human spaceflight hazards (radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, gravity fields, hostile/closed environments) into one mission dashboard. Every finding shows its rule, source label, measurement age and recommended action. The system works onboard first, then sends a role-filtered report to the ground team after the simulated signal delay. It does not diagnose, prescribe or control devices, and it is not a medical device. All mission data is synthetic.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

On long missions, communication with Earth is delayed (up to about 20 minutes one way to Mars), so crews must make health decisions on their own. ASTROBIO is an onboard mission health dashboard that shows the five NASA human spaceflight hazards (radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, gravity fields, closed environments) for the same person, day and mission in one place.

HOW IT WORKS

A deterministic rule engine compares measurements against Earth and space reference rules. Each finding shows its source label (verified, partial or demo), the measurement age and the recommended action. Role-based access separates crew, medical officer and flight surgeon on Earth. Reports sent to Earth are delivered only after a simulated signal delay (LEO, Moon, Mars scale), so the system works onboard first and transmits later. Other modules: Light and Circadian Care schedule planner, symptom self-report chat (16 categories), 90-day synthetic crew profiles, and a Live Monitoring demo stream.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Decision support stays with the crew while communication is delayed, and every value is traceable to a source and a time.

TOOLS

Node.js 24, TypeScript, SQLite, HTML/CSS/JavaScript. Optional on-device AI (MedGemma, Qwen3 via Ollama) and local speech (Whisper, Piper).

LIMITS (stated honestly)

Prototype with synthetic mission data; baseline blood-count ranges are based on NASA OSDR OSD-569. No clinical validation, no physical sensors, not a medical device. The system gives recommendations only and does not diagnose or control devices.

LIVE DEMO

https://astrobio-new-repo-1.onrender.com

Demo login: user C2, PIN 2026. The free server sleeps when idle, so the first load may take about a minute. Local AI and voice features run on-device and are not available on the hosted instance; they are shown in our demo.

SOURCE CODE

https://github.com/Tubitak-Takim/astrobio-new-repo

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) USE

Our team used SI tools (large language models such as Claude) to help draft, review and structure presentation materials and project text. The product also uses local SI models (MedGemma, Qwen3, Whisper, Piper) for optional features. No NASA logos or branding were generated or modified.
